docs.title: AnaTele
docs.text:
Evidence-first investigation of ArduPilot flight logs. AnaTele reads Mission Planner .tlog and DataFlash .bin/.log files and turns them into a reproducible investigation:

  • What happened? A timeline, armed episodes and flight phases (takeoff, pre-event window, upset, disarm).
  • Where did it go? A 3D replay of the recorded path with mission waypoints and their status.
  • What looks wrong? A versioned rule pack. Each rule is triggered, not triggered, unassessable or not applicable.
  • Why might it have happened? Hypotheses ranked by the evidence for and against each one. No invented probabilities.
  • Can I check it? Every claim links back to the exact log record and its raw bytes.
  • Can I share it? Save the whole analysis as one .ant file.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Download for Windows, macOS or Linux Source on GitHub

pip install "git+https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/AnaTele"
anatele simulate --out simulations

AnaTele gives you observations and hypotheses. It is not a crash verdict, a probability of cause or an airworthiness approval. Missing data is treated as unknown, never as healthy.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
AnaTele can be used in four ways:

Option Best for Command Standalone desktop build Pilots and investigators; no Python needed Download from Releases pip install Developers, scripting, CLI pip install "anatele[desktop] @ git+https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/AnaTele" Docker (web UI) A shared lab machine or private server docker compose up -d Source checkout Contributing pip install -e ".[desktop,dev]"

docs.title: Standalone desktop build
docs.text:
Each v* tag triggers release.yml. It builds a one-folder PyInstaller bundle for Windows, macOS and Linux and attaches it to the GitHub release together with the wheel and five simulated flights.

  1. Download AnaTele-<os>.zip and extract it.
  2. Run AnaTele.exe (Windows) or AnaTele (macOS/Linux).
  3. Open simulations/sim_motor_failure.tlog to try it.

The build is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen may ask you to confirm (More info → Run anyway); on macOS, right-click → Open.

Verifying a download. Each release includes SHA256SUMS.txt and a Sigstore-signed build-provenance attestation that ties every asset to the exact workflow run and commit that produced it:

gh attestation verify AnaTele-windows.zip --repo Avinashistoocool/AnaTele

Supply-chain hardening. Release builds install only hash-locked dependencies from requirements/release.txt (--require-hashes). Every GitHub Action is pinned to a full commit SHA, and the build jobs have a read-only token with no persisted credentials. Only a final publish job, which runs no third-party build tooling, can write to the release. To update the lock:

uv pip compile requirements/release.in --universal --python-version 3.12 --generate-hashes -o requirements/release.txt

Build locally:

pip install -e ".[desktop,dev]"
pyinstaller --noconfirm anatele.spec        # → dist/AnaTele/

The bundled executable re-invokes itself with a hidden --worker-job argument for each analysis, so workers keep the same process isolation as a source install.

docs.title: pip
docs.text:
pip install "anatele[desktop] @ git+https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/AnaTele"
anatele --help        # desktop app with no arguments; see USAGE for sub-commands

Use plain anatele (without [desktop]) on servers where Qt isn't wanted. You still get anatele web, analyse, replay and simulate.

docs.title: Docker (web UI)
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --build
# open http://127.0.0.1:8766

The compose file:

  • Publishes only on the host's loopback (127.0.0.1:8766).
  • Runs as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem, no-new-privileges and a 1 GB memory limit.
  • Stores data in the named volume anatele-data (/data).
  • Includes the simulated flights in /app/simulations (docker compose exec anatele ls /app/simulations).

Plain Docker:

docker build -t anatele .
docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:8766:8766 -v anatele-data:/data anatele

docs.title: Exposing beyond localhost
docs.text:
AnaTele has no authentication or multi-tenancy, and its parser worker is not an OS sandbox. If other people need access:

  1. Put it behind an authenticating reverse proxy (e.g. Caddy or nginx with OAuth2 Proxy, or Tailscale/Cloudflare Access).
  2. Add the public hostname to ANATELE_ALLOWED_HOSTS (comma-separated). Otherwise the Host-header check rejects requests.
  3. Keep the container on a private network. Don't publish port 8766 directly to the Internet.

Example Caddy snippet:

anatele.example.org {
    forward_auth oauth2-proxy:4180 { uri /oauth2/auth }
    reverse_proxy anatele:8766
}

docs.text:
Install Default location Source checkout ./data Installed / standalone on Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\AnaTele Installed / standalone on macOS / Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/anatele or ~/.local/share/anatele Docker /data volume

Contents: platform.db (SQLite: profiles, jobs, manifests), uploads/ (original files, never modified), datasets/<job>/ (observations and signals Parquet), worker_logs/ (parser output and tracebacks), exports/ (temporary files while the web UI streams or receives a .ant; removed afterwards). Opened .ant files become ordinary entries in datasets/, plus uploads/ when the original log was included. The desktop app and web UI can share one directory, but only one web server per directory can run at a time.

Back up by copying the directory while AnaTele is stopped. Nothing is deleted automatically; remove uploads/ and datasets/ entries yourself to reclaim space.

docs.title: Drone telemetry investigation platform
docs.text: Design baseline: 29 October 2026 Status: architecture proposal, not an implementation claim. The existing drone_telemetry.py prototype remains a CSV-only offline demonstrator.

docs.title: Executive summary
docs.text:
Build an evidence-based flight investigation workbench. Its main job is to reconstruct what the aircraft and its operator reported, distinguish observations from interpretations, rank plausible failure mechanisms, and make every claim traceable to the original records. It must not issue an unqualified crash verdict or certify that an aircraft is safe to fly.

The proposed stack is Python/FastAPI, isolated parser and analysis workers, PostgreSQL, S3-compatible immutable object storage, Parquet/DuckDB, and a React/TypeScript frontend using MapLibre and Plotly. Start with ArduPilot tlog and DataFlash support, profile/parameter provenance, a synchronized timeline, a small validated diagnostic rule pack, and evidence-linked reports. Defer arbitrary scripts, broad autopilot coverage, predictive maintenance and elaborate 3D.

The motivating incident illustrates why this distinction matters: a compass switch before a crash-check disarm is a useful association, but not proof that the compass caused the loss of control. In the inspected Copter 4.7.2 source, the reported AngErr is a thrust-vector tracking error, not a compass/yaw-error measurement.[1]

docs.title: 1. Assumptions and boundaries
docs.text:
1. The described real log has not been supplied for this design review. Its size, message counts, warnings, distances and measurements are treated as user-reported observations, not independently reproduced results.
  2. The first release is post-flight and read-only. There is no MAVLink connection to an aircraft, parameter-write endpoint, motor-control function or automated flight approval.
  3. ArduPilot is the first fully supported ecosystem. PX4 later receives a separate semantic adapter and rule pack, rather than inheriting Copter rules.
  4. Users may upload incomplete, corrupt, malicious or incorrectly labelled files.
  5. Uploaded locations, operator identities, routes and configurations are private unless deliberately shared.
  6. Human-readable firmware strings may identify an official release or a custom build. Semantics are only as trustworthy as the firmware match.
  7. Thresholds, time windows and performance budgets proposed below are design decisions unless explicitly identified as firmware behavior or documentation.
  8. A profile describes an aircraft; a log describes an observation of that aircraft at a particular time. Neither silently overrides the other.

docs.title: The central product promise
docs.text:
Turn a flight log into a reproducible incident investigation: what happened, which explanations fit, what contradicts them, and what evidence is missing.

The interface should answer these questions in order:

  1. Which aircraft, firmware, configuration and source streams are represented?
  2. Which portions of the recording are usable?
  3. What happened before, during and after each flight?
  4. Which observations indicate a problem?
  5. Which failure mechanisms are supported, and with what limitations?
  6. What additional data or safe inspection would discriminate among them?

docs.title: Different users
docs.text:
User Primary problem Product value Hobbyist or builder Many warnings, little understanding of their relationships Plain-language explanations, parameter context, precise evidence links Commercial operator Need incident triage and an operational record Repeatable reports, flight comparison, annotations and accountable review Fleet maintainer Need to distinguish a recurring hardware issue from changing flight conditions Per-aircraft histories, configuration-aware trends and maintenance records Developer or investigator Need reproducible details, not a dashboard assertion Raw record access, parser versions, full-resolution plots and competing hypotheses

Use the same evidence model for all four. Adjust presentation depth rather than maintaining an opaque simplified diagnosis for beginners.

docs.title: Facts to reconstruct versus conclusions to investigate
docs.text: Reported observation Defensible interpretation Unsupported shortcut to avoid PreArm: Radio failsafe on, throttle about 1000, threshold 975 A radio-integrity/pre-arm problem was reported; investigate its actual trigger and timing “1000 is below 975” or “the threshold caused this” GPS “unable to configure band” A receiver configuration operation was rejected “GPS had no usable fix” Auto mode not armable Arming was rejected in that mode under the active configuration “GPS caused the arming rejection” EKF compass selection changed before disarm An estimator event preceded the reported crash-check action “Changing compass caused the crash” AngErr=160>30 The crash detector reported a large thrust-vector tracking error “The compass had a 160-degree yaw error” Compasses inconsistent after both incidents Compass checks failed afterward “They were necessarily inconsistent before flight” Z vibration peak about 66 A high processed vibration value was observed “Vibration caused the crash”, without timing and persistence Clipping count 316 A counter or derived count needs sensor-instance and reset context Sum all sampled counter values and call that 316 new events Position estimate approached WP2 by 0.4 m A reported position series was close to the candidate waypoint “The aircraft physically reached it to 0.4 m accuracy”

docs.title: Critical firmware details
docs.text:
The Copter-4.7.2 tag was verified at commit fb773567896014da007bca58358704d4a0d8516f. This makes a versioned semantic pack possible, but does not establish that the user's aircraft ran that exact binary.

For that version, the crash check includes armed/not-landed and mode-related gates, filtered gravity-compensated acceleration below 3 m/s², estimated lean above 15 degrees, thrust-vector tracking error above 30 degrees, and a speed gate below 10 m/s when velocity is available. The gate must persist for a counter equivalent to nominally two seconds at the configured loop rate. The printed error is the value at triggering, not necessarily throughout the interval. The source's executable conditions should take precedence over stale comments.[1]

This is not a physical-impact detector and does not identify a failed component. The estimated attitude itself can be wrong.

For the same verified release:

  • ARMING_SKIPCHK=128 skips the board-voltage check, not compass checking. Do not decode this using a remembered ARMING_CHECK bit table.
  • BATT_MONITOR=0 disables that battery-monitor instance. Inspect additional instances before saying that all battery monitoring is absent.
  • FS_GCS_ENABLE=0 disables the GCS-heartbeat failsafe. Whether this conflicts with the intended operation depends on the control-link and mission policy.[2]

docs.title: A provisional investigation, not a numeric verdict
docs.text:
The reported observations justify investigating three competing mechanisms:

  1. Estimator/magnetic inconsistency: supported by the reported compass selection and inconsistency messages; weakened as a causal conclusion if the affected core was not primary or the disagreement appears only after impact.
  2. Mechanical/thrust-generation or configuration problem: compatible with loss of thrust-vector tracking; needs motor mapping, target-versus-estimated attitude, ESC evidence and inspection. Apparently successful takeoff is context to consider, not a conclusive exclusion.
  3. Vibration-driven estimation degradation: plausible only if excessive vibration/clipping is shown before the loss of control, not just at impact.

The radio/pre-arm failures should be a separate finding group. They may share underlying electrical issues, but that relationship must be demonstrated. The platform should not assign numerical root-cause probabilities from this description alone.

docs.title: 4. Recommended system architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    U[Browser / operator] --> API[FastAPI: auth, metadata, upload coordination]
    API --> PG[(PostgreSQL: jobs, profiles, events, findings, audit)]
    API --> UP[Restricted multipart upload session]
    UP --> RAW[(Quarantined object storage)]
    PG --> S[Job scheduler: leases and retries]
    S --> P[Isolated file parser]
    RAW --> P
    P --> N[Normalize identities, clocks, units, parameters]
    N --> PAR[(Immutable Parquet + dataset manifest)]
    N --> PG
    PAR --> A[Analysis worker: DuckDB + typed rules]
    PG --> A
    A --> F[Evidence graph and ranked hypotheses]
    F --> PG
    API --> Q[Bounded series-query workers]
    PAR --> Q
    Q --> API
    API --> UI[React: timeline, map, plots, evidence panel]
    PG --> R[Versioned report renderer]
    PAR --> R
    R --> REP[(PDF / shareable report artifacts)]

docs.title: Technology choices
docs.text:
Layer Recommendation Reason API FastAPI, Python, typed request/response models Same language as parsers and analysis; explicit contracts Job scheduling PostgreSQL job table with leased workers One operational datastore initially; durable retries and audit Parsing Pinned pymavlink adapters; pyulog for later ULog support Existing format implementations, wrapped by platform validation Raw/derived artifacts S3-compatible versioned storage Immutable source and output references; large files kept out of SQL Metadata PostgreSQL Transactions, tenant isolation, structured relationships Bulk samples Parquet grouped by dataset and signal family Efficient bounded interval and column reads Analysis/query engine DuckDB in separate resource-limited workers SQL over Parquet without introducing a distributed analytics cluster Frontend React + TypeScript, MapLibre, Plotly Linked investigation panels, maps and engineering plots First deployment Docker Compose, separate API/scheduler/worker services Easier operation than Kubernetes while retaining isolation boundaries

Heavy parsing is not a FastAPI in-process background task. It belongs in a separate worker with resource limits and a durable job record.[14]

Use at-least-once execution with idempotent outputs, not an “exactly once” claim. An analysis identity includes input manifest, profile snapshot, semantic pack, rule-set hash, analysis configuration and engine version.

docs.title: Job lifecycle
docs.text:
created -> uploading -> upload_verified -> parsing -> normalizing
        -> analysis_queued -> analyzing -> publishing -> complete

There are explicit failed, cancelled, and partial_dataset outcomes. An interrupted upload is not the same as a fully received but truncated log. Publish a dataset manifest only after its referenced files pass integrity checks; failed work must not appear as a complete analysis.

docs.title: 5. Data model
docs.text:
Avoid one table called flights containing everything.

Entity Purpose and important fields Tenant / user / membership Ownership, roles, permissions, audit actor Drone Stable physical asset ID; not simply MAVLink system ID ProfileVersion Frame, propulsion, sensors, firmware, operating policy, effective interval, provenance SourceArtifact Hash, original name, size, object version, format, acquisition metadata ParseRun / DatasetVersion Parser/dialect hashes, diagnostics, clock mappings, coverage inventory, Parquet manifests SourceIdentity System/component IDs, topic instance, candidate role, link evidence, boot epoch RecordingSession Capture session that can contain several aircraft, reboots or flights ArmedEpisode Armed interval, possibly entirely on the ground FlightEpisode Observed/inferred takeoff and landing intervals, confidence, vehicle and clock epoch ParameterObservation Name, typed raw/decoded value, instance, source, requested/reported distinction ParameterSnapshot Values and completeness evidence at a time; missing indices and conflicts MissionTransaction / MissionVersion Direction, participants, mission type, items, acceptance evidence and uncertainty Observation Typed measurement, raw source locator, original time, normalized time, units and quality Event / EventEpisode Individual transitions/warnings and derived grouped occurrences RuleVersion Applicability, requirements, typed logic, thresholds, tests, validation status, content hash RuleEvaluation Triggered, not triggered, unassessable, or not applicable; coverage and reasons Finding / Hypothesis Claim, severity, support, contradictions, unknowns, ranking and evidence AnalysisRun Exact immutable inputs, rule versions, engine image, options and execution status Annotation / MaintenanceAction Human interpretation, inspected component, corrective action, eventual outcome Report / Share Versioned output, redactions, access scope, expiry and revocation

docs.title: Format detection and isolation
docs.text:
Use explicit file-only adapters:

adapters\ardupilot_tlog
adapters\ardupilot_dataflash
adapters\px4_ulog
adapters\mapped_csv

Inspect file signatures and record structure, not just the extension. Pymavlink's convenience dispatcher is not a universal detector: it includes network/device transports and other behaviors that an upload API should never expose. Do not pass an arbitrary user string into that dispatcher.[3]

Run parsers with no network or credentials, read-only staged input, isolated scratch storage, and CPU, memory, process, output-size and wall-time budgets. Reject unsupported incompatibility flags. Keep the original file even when salvaging its usable records.

docs.title: Mission Planner tlog
docs.text:
The inspected Mission Planner writer prefixes packet bytes with an eight-byte big-endian Unix-epoch microsecond timestamp. It records both outgoing and incoming traffic, so call this capture/write time rather than assuming it is always a sensor receive time.[4]

Preserve the prefix bytes. Pymavlink exposes low timestamp bits as a link value, but the inspected Mission Planner writer does not explicitly reserve them. Do not treat that decoded value as proof of multiple physical links for every Mission Planner recording.[3][4]

docs.title: MAVLink validation
docs.text:
Classify every frame as validated, truncated, CRC-failed, signature-unverified, signature-failed, unknown-definition, or unsupported-framing as appropriate. CRC validity is not authentication. A present signature is not a verified signature without the necessary validation context.

Robust parsing can return bad-data records; it does not repair information. Unknown message definitions may be retained by a parser without undergoing the same checks as known messages. Store unknown payloads and offsets so a later dialect version can reinterpret them.[3][5]

For MAVLink2, distinguish valid trailing-zero payload truncation from an incomplete/corrupted frame. Preserve whether optional fields were actually available before treating a decoded default as a physical measurement.

docs.title: Identities and message loss
docs.text:
Use sender system/component IDs, available link provenance, and boot/session identity. Separate source from command target. Identify the flight-controller stream through heartbeat type/autopilot and corroborating messages, not “ID 1 must be the drone.” A single recording can contain relayed duplicates, GCS heartbeats, radio reports and more than one aircraft.[5]

Sequence numbers wrap at 256. Evaluate continuity only within defensible source/channel/session streams. A gap does not uniquely prove radio loss: filtering, forwarding, reordering and mixed channels also matter. Report a conditional loss estimate with its assumptions rather than a universal “packet loss percentage.”

docs.title: STATUSTEXT
docs.text:
Reassemble long MAVLink2 text using sender/session/message ID and chunk sequence. Preserve partial or conflicting assemblies. Reconstruct bytes before decoding UTF-8 so a character split across chunks is not corrupted.[5]

Store every warning occurrence. A UI episode such as “Radio failsafe ×47 across 4 minutes” is a derived view, not 47 independent confirmations and not proof that a failsafe flag remained continuously asserted for all four minutes.

docs.title: DataFlash, ULog and CSV
docs.text:
DataFlash adapters retain embedded format, unit, multiplier and instance definitions. Preserve native boot timestamps even if a parser supplies a derived wall-clock timestamp. PX4 ULog uses its own formats, subscription IDs, instances and dropout records; do not force these into fake MAVLink IDs.[3][6]

CSV import requires an explicit mapping for timestamps, timezone/domain, identity, units and null values. Never execute user-supplied timestamp expressions. Units inferred from column names should remain suggestions pending confirmation.

docs.title: 7. Clock model and synchronization
docs.text:
Maintain at least:

  1. Capture clock.
  2. Vehicle boot clock.
  3. GPS/UTC clock when usable.
  4. Derived investigation clock with mapping uncertainty.

SYSTEM_TIME can provide boot/Unix relationships. Some timestamp fields permit either boot-relative or epoch values; interpretation must follow the message definition, not one global heuristic.[5]

Segment credible reboot epochs. Distinguish reboot, delayed delivery and 32-bit boot-millisecond wrap. Record inconsistent anchors and clock jumps. Capture minus sensor time is not automatically network latency.

When combining onboard and telemetry logs, align through multiple shared landmarks and clock anchors, retain residual error, and make an uncertain match visible. Two records separated by five seconds in display time may not have a defensible causal order if the alignment uncertainty is larger.

Never interpolate across reboot, estimator-origin reset, long data gaps or incompatible frames. Hold discrete states between observations with a visible freshness limit. Interpolated chart points must never masquerade as original evidence.

docs.title: 8. Profile and parameter audit
docs.text:
Build this early: diagnostic thresholds and applicability depend on it.

A profile should contain:

  • Frame class/type and motor geometry.
  • Motor/ESC/propeller specifications and channel-function mapping where known.
  • Firmware name/version, git identity, board and build information.
  • Sensor instances, orientations, device IDs and intended estimator sources.
  • Battery chemistry/cell count/capacity and monitor assignments.
  • Intended control links and failsafe policy.
  • Payload and typical operating envelope.
  • Maintenance changes, configuration versions and known limitations.

Each field records whether it is operator-declared, firmware-reported, inferred or externally verified. “Quadrotor” in a heartbeat does not alone identify an X-frame geometry, and a generic GPS message does not establish a u-blox model.

docs.title: Parameter completeness
docs.text:
973 observed names does not prove a full snapshot. Track param_count, index coverage, sender component, request/response context, repeated values and changes within a collection epoch. A snapshot can be complete, partial, internally inconsistent or of unknown completeness.[7]

Separate a requested PARAM_SET from a reported PARAM_VALUE. Decode the advertised parameter type and supported value encoding; preserve raw bytes. Do not treat an unacknowledged request as an effective configuration change. For restart-required parameters, reported stored value and active runtime value may differ; retain that uncertainty.

docs.title: Audits and comparisons
docs.text:
Version parameter metadata by exact firmware where possible. Diff changes in value, type, meaning, availability and completeness. Do not report a missing parameter in a partial snapshot as “reset to default.”

A known-good preset is a scoped reference, not a universal safety certificate: it needs frame, hardware, firmware, payload/mission assumptions, provenance, validation owner and expiry/review state. Show why a mismatch matters. Never automatically apply a preset or disable arming checks.

docs.title: Stage A: establish observations and operating context
docs.text:
Before ranking causes, reconstruct:

  • Vehicle/source and boot identity.
  • Armed episodes versus observed/inferred airborne flights.
  • Mode, mission and parameter state.
  • Available channels, rates, gaps and invalid samples.
  • Relevant pre-arm, takeoff, transition, flight, landing and post-event phases.

An armed vehicle on a bench is not automatically an airborne flight. Use flight-controller heartbeat and landed-state reports where present; otherwise label phase estimates and their uncertainty.[8]

docs.title: Stage B: derive events and indicators
docs.text:
Examples: an arming rejection, a compass-selection change, a rise in clipping, sustained tracking error, a voltage sag, a command-output plateau.

Use full-resolution observations for detection. A plot's downsampled line is not the input to the diagnostic engine.

docs.title: Stage C: evaluate hypothesis rules
docs.text:
id: compass-switch-before-crash-check
version: 1
semantic_pack: arducopter-4.7.2
requires:
  events:
    - crash_check_disarm
    - ekf_compass_selection_change
  context:
    - vehicle_identity
    - clock_epoch
    - flight_episode
correlate:
  same_vehicle: true
  same_epoch: true
  before_seconds: 20
support:
  - compass_change_in_active_ekf_core
  - magnetic_innovation_failure_before_tracking_loss
contradictions:
  - first_attitude_failure_precedes_compass_change
  - changed_core_not_primary
unknowns:
  - missing_primary_core_identity
  - missing_magnetic_innovations
output:
  observed_pattern: compass_event_before_crash_check
  hypotheses:
    - magnetic_estimation_problem
    - vibration_related_estimator_degradation
  probability: null

This is an illustrative DSL, not executed firmware logic. Its 20-second correlation window is a proposed screening window, not a documented causal threshold.

Rule results have four states: triggered, not_triggered, unassessable, not_applicable. A failed applicability or coverage check is not a healthy result.

docs.title: Stage D: rank without pretending to know probabilities
docs.text:
Start with an explainable, expert-reviewed ranking:

rank(H) =
    configured prior weight
  + capped support from each evidence family
  - explicit contradictory evidence

Evidence families might be magnetic/estimator, inertial/vibration, propulsion, power, navigation and communications. Source integrity, timestamp uncertainty, phase relevance and sampling coverage govern whether evidence is usable.

Do not count every repeated STATUSTEXT message, derivative feature and plot summary as independent support. Do not treat two flights on the same hardware and configuration as independent laboratory replications.

Display four separate concepts:

  • Severity if the mechanism is real.
  • Comparative investigation priority.
  • Evidence completeness/quality.
  • Calibrated probability, only if validated for that task and population.

Initially use labels such as strong support, mixed support and limited evidence with explanations, not “92% compass failure.” Future probability calibration requires adjudicated outcomes and held-out evaluation.

docs.title: Stage E: recommend discriminating evidence and safe actions
docs.text:
For every hypothesis, answer:

What observation would most clearly distinguish this from its nearest rival?

Examples are onboard magnetic innovations, measured ESC RPM/current, a complete parameter snapshot, or qualified inspection of mounting and propulsion. Post-crash recommendations should prioritize safe, propellers-removed inspection and review of existing evidence—not another Auto flight or force-arming.

docs.title: 10. Eight concrete rule designs
docs.text: The persistence windows below are initial configurable analysis choices. Firmware gates are separately versioned and must not be confused with them.

docs.title: Rule 1: repeated pre-arm radio-integrity failure
docs.text:
• Trigger: repeated Radio failsafe on warnings or an explicitly observed failsafe state during a pre-arm episode.
  • Evidence: mapped throttle input, RCMAP_THROTTLE, calibration, reversal, freshness, receiver failsafe indications, RC options, override activity and timeout settings.
  • Logic: distinguish below-threshold input, lost valid updates and receiver/ override-related mechanisms. In the motivating report, 1000 exceeds 975, so those samples do not establish the below-threshold mechanism.
  • Exclusions: GCS-origin RC messages, old retained values, sparse observations that cannot demonstrate fresh receiver updates.
  • Output: an arming blocker with unresolved or supported trigger branches, not a fabricated adjustment to FS_THR_VALUE.

Copter's channel state can include overrides; streamed RC values are not an independent capture of the receiver wire protocol.[9]

docs.title: Rule 2: arming rejected by mode or throttle state
docs.text:
• Trigger: Auto mode not armable or Throttle too high.
  • Evidence: exact firmware semantics, current mode, arming-command method, Auto options, calibrated throttle/control demand and contemporaneous warnings.
  • Logic: assess each rejected attempt separately. Copter 4.7.2 has an Auto allow-arming option and mode-specific conditions; throttle-high checking is different from low-throttle failsafe.
  • Exclusions: an old mission upload or GPS configuration message merely appearing nearby.
  • Output: distinct rejection reasons, not a single “GPS arming failure.”

The GPS band warning should create a configuration warning whose operational impact remains conditional on actual fix/accuracy and estimator acceptance.[9]

docs.title: Rule 3: estimator/compass event before crash-check disarm
docs.text:
• Trigger: correctly classified compass/core/yaw event within a proposed 20-second pre-disarm window.
  • Evidence: exact warning text, active EKF core, compass device mapping, innovations, target/estimated attitude, current and vibration history.
  • Logic: distinguish compass selection, EKF lane switch, yaw-source change and yaw reset. Record onset ordering relative to tracking deterioration.
  • Exclusions: inactive-core-only changes; post-impact disagreement used as proof of pre-impact failure; correlation based on uncertain clocks.
  • Output: supported chronology and competing hypotheses. Mark any causal interpretation as limited when internal EKF evidence is unavailable.

Compass switching may be an estimator recovery action rather than the initiating fault.[10]

docs.title: Rule 4: loss of thrust-vector tracking
docs.text:
• Trigger: controller/estimate divergence sustained for a configurable 0.5–1 second screening interval, or an observed crash-check disarm message.
  • Evidence: target and estimated orientation, body rates, outputs, filtered acceleration, speed and exact detector semantics.
  • Logic: distinguish an implausible target, a state-estimate jump, and failure to follow a plausible target. Reproduce internal crash gates only if the necessary signals and sampling permit it.
  • Exclusions: mismatched coordinate frames, comparing unaligned signals, treating AngErr as full yaw error.
  • Output: a tracking failure; possible control, estimation and thrust causes remain separate.

For Copter 4.7.2, use the thrust-vector definition and executable crash gates.[1]

docs.title: Rule 5: sustained vibration and accelerometer clipping
docs.text:
• Trigger: initial screening above 30 m/s² for 2 seconds, above 60 m/s² for 1 second, or positive clipping increments in airborne pre-event intervals.
  • Evidence: per-instance vibration and clipping, boot boundaries, sample intervals and phase.
  • Logic: calculate positive counter increments within a valid epoch; report increments over known intervals rather than inventing individual clip times.
  • Exclusions: impact/handling-only peaks, counter resets, mixed IMU instances, and summing cumulative samples.
  • Output: pre-event vibration exposure, impact-only exposure or insufficient temporal evidence.

ArduPilot's documentation gives 30/60 as useful vibration guidance, not universal crash thresholds. Its vibration metric is filtered, not instantaneous acceleration. DataFlash instance fields differ from MAVLink's clipping0/1/2 representation, so the semantic adapter must normalize them.[11]

docs.title: Rule 6: abnormal propulsion-command distribution
docs.text:
• Trigger: output imbalance/saturation persisting in a comparable, nominally steady phase; initially use a configurable two-second screening interval.
  • Evidence: actual channel-function mapping, frame geometry, output limits, desired attitude/rates, achieved motion, ESC RPM/current where available.
  • Logic: compare outputs with expected control demands, not just their spread.
  • Exclusions: takeoff transients, aggressive maneuvers, yaw commands, wind, asymmetric payload and different mixer configurations.
  • Output: command-distribution anomaly. Without measured motor response or inspection, do not claim a particular motor/propeller has failed.

Motor commands are not measured thrust. Wrong geometry/order/direction requires additional corroboration.

docs.title: Rule 7: power monitoring gap or voltage anomaly
docs.text:
• Trigger A: no usable propulsion battery or board-supply observations for the operating policy.
  • Trigger B: sustained sag/undervoltage against an appropriate configured threshold with valid current/load context.
  • Evidence: all monitor instances, voltage/current, board supply, resets, battery profile and arming-check configuration.
  • Logic: separate an observability defect from observed power degradation.
  • Exclusions: invalid sentinels, disconnected/unused monitor instances, chemistry/cell-count mismatch and sparse unaligned current measurements.
  • Output: monitoring coverage gap, observed voltage anomaly, or unassessable battery condition. ARMING_SKIPCHK=128 is contextual risk in the verified firmware, not proof of an electrical cause.[2]

docs.title: Rule 8: communication/navigation policy mismatch
docs.text:
• Trigger: required RC/GCS/GNSS service becomes unavailable, or configured failsafe behavior contradicts the declared operating policy.
  • Evidence: relevant source freshness, explicit failsafe events, GCS role, RC availability, mode, mission policy, fix/accuracy and estimator use.
  • Logic: distinguish a radio's status report from actual vehicle link health and a GNSS configuration warning from failed positioning.
  • Exclusions: optional GCS loss during a deliberately permitted autonomous mission; message absence when a topic was never streamed.
  • Output: actionable policy mismatch or loss evidence, not “unsafe because FS_GCS_ENABLE is zero.”

docs.title: Treat uploads as transactions with uncertain outcomes
docs.text:
Recognize the direction of MISSION_COUNT, requests, items and ACKs. An upload and a download can carry similar messages in opposite directions. Retransmissions are not automatically new plans.[12]

Maintain separate:

  1. GCS-intended mission versions.
  2. Observed upload/download transactions.
  3. Acceptance evidence.
  4. Inferred/confirmed onboard mission state.
  5. Execution observations.

A confirmed shorter full upload replaces the earlier plan; do not keep old trailing points. Partial writes need a known baseline. The MAVLink documentation notes non-atomic ArduPilot upload behavior; therefore, do not guarantee that the last accepted mission remains onboard after an interrupted overwrite. Model possible partial modification unless the exact firmware/transaction evidence establishes otherwise.[12]

Use available opaque plan IDs as corroboration, not universal identifiers. Missing or zero extension fields do not establish plan identity.

docs.title: Reached versus observed near
docs.text:
Use explicit statuses:

reported_complete
geometry_consistent_with_completion
completion_not_observed
not_visited_in_observed_trajectory
unassessable

Store the command itself. A takeoff item is not an ordinary horizontal waypoint. ArduPilot commonly uses sequence zero for home; never relabel by display order without retaining original sequence numbers.[12]

A missing MISSION_ITEM_REACHED does not prove failure to reach, and a MISSION_CURRENT advance can reflect a jump or set-current operation. Generic MAVLink waypoint fields do not guarantee that a given Copter release implements each field. In particular, do not invent a universal waypoint yaw acceptance condition.[12][13]

For the reported 0.4 m approach, show:

  • Candidate mission version and item command/frame.
  • Nearest recorded horizontal distance.
  • Vertical error only when frames/datums are compatible.
  • GPS/estimator uncertainty and observation gap.
  • Whether interpolation was used.
  • Whether an execution completion message was observed.

Call the 21.6 m value a recorded-position distance to a waypoint unless an along-path definition and correct active plan are established.

docs.title: Geometry and mission warnings
docs.text:
Distinguish MSL, ellipsoid, home-relative and terrain-relative altitude. Home-relative altitude is not generally AGL. Preserve local NED/ENU and body FRD semantics; local frames require a known origin. GPS course is not vehicle heading, and the estimated global position is not physical ground truth.[5][13]

Cross-track distance must name its reference: a straight mission segment is not the controller's curved/spline path. Plan-level battery margin is unassessable without sufficient battery/energy observations and a validated load model; distance alone is not a credible energy estimate.

docs.title: Investigation screen
docs.text:
Use one time-selection model shared by:

  • Severity-filtered event timeline.
  • Map and planned/flown path.
  • Linked engineering plots.
  • Parameter changes and flight-phase markers.
  • Hypothesis cards with support/contradictions.
  • Raw record/evidence inspector.

Clicking a finding selects its interval and opens the exact source records plus bounded before/after context. A warning episode expands to individual messages. Show missing/invalid data as gaps, not zeros.

Compare flights by elapsed time from takeoff or equivalent mission phase while retaining actual timestamps and durations. Do not automatically equate “WP2” between different mission versions.

docs.title: 3D
docs.text: Start with correct 2D and altitude plots. Later add 3D with explicit altitude datum and frame conversion. Interpolate quaternions with sign continuity; unwrap displayed angles and stop interpolation at gaps/resets. A visually smooth trajectory must not imply more accurate measurements.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Each report includes:

  1. Scope, aircraft/profile identity, firmware match and data limitations.
  2. Observed incident sequence.
  3. Ranked hypotheses and supporting/contradicting evidence.
  4. Parameter and monitoring concerns.
  5. Missing evidence and recommended safe follow-up.
  6. Analysis/rule versions and immutable evidence links.

An optional LLM can phrase already-approved structured findings. It must not invent diagnoses, thresholds, source citations or repair instructions. Log strings are untrusted input and must not become model instructions. Provide a deterministic report fallback.

docs.title: 13. Fleet trends and maintenance
docs.text:
First implement condition trends, not remaining-useful-life claims.

Compare like-for-like flight phases while accounting for:

  • Firmware/profile revisions and sensor replacement.
  • Payload, battery identity, temperature and environment.
  • Maneuver intensity, duration and recording rates.
  • Sensor instances, units and signal coverage.

A vibration trend is not automatically motor wear. Motor wear needs appropriate response measurements and maintenance outcomes. Battery degradation needs consistent battery identity and comparable charge/load/temperature conditions. Record maintenance actions, replaced parts, inspection findings and subsequent flights so useful labels can accumulate.

Do not compare a sparse radio log with a high-rate onboard log as if their peaks and counter visibility were directly equivalent.

docs.title: MVP: a bounded DSL
docs.text:
Allow registered signals, comparisons, durations, aggregates, temporal joins, exclusions and templated evidence. Validate units, expected types, applicable firmware and required coverage at rule creation.

Every shared rule needs a version/hash, author, tests, description, applicability, known confounders, validation state and review history. A tenant pins a rule version; publishing an update must not silently rewrite old investigations.

docs.title: Later: isolated executable extensions
docs.text: Do not execute user Python in the API or privileged analysis process. If scripts become necessary, use reviewed immutable packages in disposable sandboxes: no network, no secrets, read-only scoped inputs, strict CPU/RAM/process/output budgets, deadlines and validated result schemas. Do not expose a container-engine socket. Hostile public plugins need stronger isolation than ordinary shared containers before launch.

docs.title: Four test layers
docs.text:
1. Parser fixtures: valid formats, wrong suffixes, truncated frames, missing chunks, unknown messages, CRC/signature states, reboots and corrupted regions.
  2. Semantic fixtures: version-specific parameter bitmasks, message units, instance mappings, time anchors, arming versus airborne state, mission retransmission/partial-write behavior.
  3. Diagnostic fixtures: positive cases, healthy counterexamples, missing channels, contradictory evidence and known confounders.
  4. End-to-end investigations: immutable expected event sequences, evidence locators, findings and report versions.

The motivating log should become a manually annotated regression case, ideally paired with its onboard logs and inspection outcome. Do not make it the entire evaluation set.

docs.title: Ground-truth levels
docs.text:
Distinguish hardware-confirmed causes, expert-adjudicated interpretations and weak labels from operator narratives. Do not train or score “root cause” against an unverified description as if it were ground truth.

Include healthy flights, recoveries, aborted takeoffs, bench activity and benign warnings—not only crashes. Split by aircraft/operator and time; keep duplicate recordings and related flights out of opposing splits.

Measure:

  • False alerts per flight-hour and per flight phase.
  • Precision/recall of observable events.
  • Top-k hypothesis recall on adjudicated incidents.
  • Correctness of cited evidence and timeline order.
  • Abstention and coverage when signals are missing.
  • Calibration only for outputs that claim probabilities.
  • Analyst time to identify and verify a useful explanation.

A high recall model that blames a compass on every crash is not a useful product.

docs.title: 16. Security, privacy and operational reliability
docs.text:
• Tenant authorization must follow every data/evidence relationship.
  • Treat parser code as exposed to hostile files. Sandbox and fuzz it.
  • Validate actual file sizes and content; bound expansion if archives are later accepted. Do not trust filenames, MIME types or client-reported hashes.
  • Use unique immutable object versions; object-store multipart ETags are not a substitute for the platform's chosen integrity hash.
  • Keep tenant-scoped caches and deduplication semantics to avoid exposing another tenant's upload or analysis.
  • Redact home coordinates, routes, identities and timestamps where required. Redaction must cover PDFs, metadata, downloadable artifacts and maps, not just visible text.
  • Use revocable application-level share tokens with narrow scope and expiry. Issue short-lived object URLs only after authorization; presigned storage URLs are bearer credentials and may be reused until expiry.[15]
  • Define deletion across raw data, Parquet, indexes, caches, reports, shares and backups; state backup-retention limits clearly.
  • Maintain access logs, restore tests and incident procedures.
  • Explain third-party map/LLM processing. Offer a no-external-services workflow for sensitive logs.

docs.title: 17. Performance and large-log design
docs.text:
Define test workloads rather than inventing performance claims:

Workload What to measure Roughly 55,000-message tlog Time to first useful preview and final analysis Ten-million-message onboard dataset Parse throughput, peak RAM and scratch storage 1 GB interrupted upload Resume behavior, integrity validation and cleanup Multiple tenants Queue fairness, cancellation and query latency under load Corrupt/high-cardinality data Resource ceilings, bounded recovery and useful error output

Stream records in bounded batches. Do not retain millions of Python message objects or emit one JSON blob per full flight to the browser. Group Parquet by dataset/signal family with suitable row groups; avoid one tiny file per message type or sensor sample.

Series-query requests specify allowlisted channels, interval, source, quality policy and point budget. Enforce bytes-scanned, execution-time and output caps. Use min/max envelopes or other spike-preserving chart summaries, with exact evidence windows fetched on demand. Analysis operates on full-resolution data, with sufficient pre/post overlap at chunk boundaries.

Cache by tenant, dataset/time-mapping version, channels, interval, aggregation and redaction policy. Benchmark on explicitly stated hardware before promising interactive latencies.

docs.title: Milestone 0: establish the evidence contract
docs.text:
• Obtain permitted, representative logs and paired onboard/telemetry recordings.
  • Annotate the motivating case without assuming its cause.
  • Freeze canonical identity, time, provenance and quality semantics.
  • Define firmware-match and data-coverage policies.

Exit: two analysts can distinguish observations, interpretations and unknowns in the same case without relying on screenshots alone.

docs.title: Milestone 1: reliable ArduPilot ingestion
docs.text:
• Tlog and DataFlash adapters, immutable artifacts and job lifecycle.
  • Source-role inventory, clock epochs, corrupt-region diagnostics.
  • Parameters/profile snapshots and channel coverage.

Exit: accepted input is reproducible and every normalized record can be traced to its original artifact; partial data cannot appear complete.

docs.title: Milestone 2: investigation UI and baseline health
docs.text:
• Armed/airborne episodes, warning grouping, mode/failsafe timeline.
  • 2D planned/flown map, linked plots and exact evidence navigation.
  • Basic mission-transaction history and version-aware parameter audit.
  • Vibration, radio, tracking and monitoring checks.

Exit: the motivating case can be investigated end to end without a generated root-cause verdict.

docs.title: Milestone 3: diagnostic MVP
docs.text:
• A small expert-reviewed rule pack covering the eight patterns above, initially prioritizing radio pre-arm failure, vibration/clipping, tracking loss and compass-event association.
  • Hypothesis ranking with contradictions and abstention.
  • Versioned operator reports and manual annotations.
  • Regression corpus including benign and missing-data cases.

MVP acceptance: on the motivating case, correctly distinguish the 1000/975 issue, interpret crash AngErr, avoid summing clipping counters, distinguish takeoff from waypoint commands, and avoid treating absent completion telemetry as definitive non-completion. Every finding has evidence and limitations.

docs.title: Milestone 4: operational hardening and expansion
docs.text:
• Tenant isolation, access/retention controls, quotas, recoverability and benchmark budgets before accepting broad external uploads.
  • PX4 ULog with its own semantic/rule pack; explicit CSV mapping.
  • Cross-flight comparisons, improved 3D and maintenance records.

docs.title: Milestone 5: outcome-driven learning
docs.text:
• Fleet condition trends and validated maintenance outcomes.
  • Optional learned hypothesis ranking or evidence prioritization.
  • Calibrated probabilities only if supported by held-out data.

If time is short, cut arbitrary scripts, LLM narratives, public rule marketplaces, live telemetry, predictive-maintenance claims and sophisticated 3D first. Do not cut provenance, profile/version awareness, data-quality reporting, counterexample tests or the distinction between unknown and healthy.

docs.title: 19. Important challenges to the original plan
docs.text:
1. Move profile/parameter handling forward. It is a dependency of trustworthy health and root-cause rules, not a later cosmetic feature.
  2. Treat mission reconstruction as state estimation. Interrupted uploads and missing messages can make the active plan genuinely unknowable.
  3. Do not equate warning order with causality. Recovery actions often occur after a problem has already begun.
  4. A tlog cannot supply information never streamed. Requesting onboard data is sometimes the correct product output.
  5. “100% analyzed” must not mean “all subsystems healthy.” Publish a capability and coverage matrix alongside every report.
  6. Frame and sensor identity are temporal. Components can be replaced; an IMU index is not a permanent physical identity.
  7. A baseline may already be unhealthy. Personalized thresholds need reviewed reference flights, not just the aircraft's historical average.
  8. A smooth 3D replay can be misleading. Keep uncertainty and missing data visible; graphics do not strengthen the underlying measurement.
  9. Root-cause labels are expensive. Maintenance/inspection outcomes and expert review are core product data, not optional future polish.
  10. Models are optional, evidence is not. A System-One classifier may later help prioritize reviewed evidence; it should not replace exact protocol reconstruction or invent causal certainty.

docs.title: Source notes
docs.text:
The report combines architectural recommendations with primary-source checks. Version-specific crash/parameter interpretations use the verified Copter 4.7.2 release source; the aircraft's actual binary is still unverified. General mission documentation and current source examples require matching against that binary before exact execution predicates are asserted.

[1] ArduPilot Copter 4.7.2: crash detector, attitude-control interface, thrust/attitude calculations.

[2] Copter 4.7.2: arming metadata, battery parameters, failsafe handling.

[3] Pymavlink at bd0a1b29d5b8b54b7d66abfe9ac043c528ac490f: mavutil dispatch/log parsing, generated-parser behavior, DataFlash reader.

[4] Mission Planner timestamp writer and recording; telemetry-log scope.

[5] MAVLink serialization, message definitions, routing, signing.

[6] PX4 ULog specification; pyulog implementation.

[7] MAVLink parameter protocol.

[8] MAVLink heartbeat and landed state.

[9] Copter 4.7.2 radio handling, arming checks, Auto arming, RC channel state, u-blox configuration handling.

[10] Copter 4.7.2 EKF compass selection, EKF primary-core handling, compass consistency.

[11] ArduPilot vibration guidance; Copter 4.7.2 vibration calculation and DataFlash definitions.

[12] MAVLink mission protocol, including ArduPilot-specific notes.

[13] ArduPilot mission-command behavior and Auto mode.

[14] FastAPI background-task caveat.

[15] AWS presigned URL behavior.

docs.title: Diagnostics reference
docs.text:
How AnaTele turns records into findings and ranked hypotheses, and how to read each result.

  • Principles
  • Pipeline
  • Flight phases
  • Rule states
  • Rule catalogue
  • Hypothesis ranking
  • Mission statuses
  • Firmware semantic packs
  • Data-quality diagnostics
  • Writing a rule
  • Known limitations

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Observations and interpretations stay separate. A STATUSTEXT saying "Crash: Disarming" is an observation. "A motor failed" would be an interpretation, and AnaTele never states it as fact.
  2. Every finding carries evidence (record ids, linked to raw bytes) and a list of what is missing to strengthen it.
  3. Missing data means unknown. If a rule can't answer, it says unassessable. It never says "OK".
  4. No probabilities without labelled outcomes. Hypotheses get a screening order and a label, not a percentage.
  5. Firmware meaning is versioned. For example, Copter 4.7.2 AngErr is a thrust-vector tracking error, not a yaw error, and ARMING_SKIPCHK bit 7 skips the board-voltage check, not the compass check.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
file ──► parser (CRC, resync, limits) ──► observations (Parquet, byte offsets)
     ──► sources & roles, clock epochs, STATUSTEXT reassembly
     ──► events (arm, mode, text classes, EKF flags, mission, parameter changes)
     ──► signals (normalised) ──► derived: motor mapping, tilt error, mixer axes
     ──► flight phases per armed episode
     ──► rule pack (rules/core.yaml) ──► findings + rule-coverage table
     ──► hypothesis ranking per crash episode
     ──► missions: transactions → plan versions → item execution
     ──► manifest (hashes, versions, limitations)

Diagnosis always uses full-resolution observations. Plot envelopes are never used.

docs.title: Flight phases
docs.text:
For each armed episode (from the vehicle HEARTBEAT armed flag, or DataFlash ARM):

Status Meaning airborne_reported EXTENDED_SYS_STATE reported In air or Taking off. airborne_inferred Home-relative altitude rose ≥ 1 m above the median of the first 2 s, and throttle ≥ 10 % or a motor output ≥ 25 % appeared within 5 s before the rise. Takeoff is backdated to the last sample ≤ 0.2 m above baseline. no_airborne_evidence Armed, but no qualifying rise. A very low hover can't be told apart from estimate noise. unassessable No home-relative altitude in the episode.

Derived times:

  • Attitude excursion: first |roll| or |pitch| > 60° after takeoff (a possible loss of control or impact).
  • Pre-event window: from takeoff to the earlier of the excursion and crash report − 3 s. Rules that ask "was this happening before the upset?" use this window.
  • Event and after: from the end of the pre-event window to disarm. It is used for contrast, e.g. "vibration 66 at impact, 24 before".

All thresholds are recorded in each phase's config. They are analysis choices, not firmware behaviour.

docs.title: Rule states
docs.text: State Meaning triggered The condition was met. Becomes a finding with evidence. not_triggered The data was adequate and the condition was not met. This is not a health certificate. unassessable The data couldn't answer: signals missing, too few samples, or a sample interval too coarse for the persistence criterion. not_applicable The question doesn't apply (e.g. a ground-only episode, or no expected parameters in the profile).

docs.title: Rule catalogue
docs.text:
Rules live in telemetry_platform/rules/core.yaml (pack core, version 2). Scopes: event (one result per anchor event), source, episode (per armed episode), series, snapshot (parameter set).

Rule id Scope Detector Triggers when crash-check-disarm event event_present A crash-check disarm message is recorded. Firmware note explains AngErr. compass-event-before-crash-check event event_sequence Compass selection, EKF lane switch or yaw reset ≤ 20 s before a crash report. Supported by compass ratio > 1 for ≥ 2 s before it; contradicted if tilt error > 30° for ≥ 0.5 s came first. prearm-radio-failsafe source event_present "PreArm: Radio failsafe". Adds the mapped throttle channel (rc.ch{RCMAP_THROTTLE}) near each report, compared with FS_THR_VALUE. arming-rejected-auto-mode source event_present "Auto mode not armable". arming-rejected-throttle-high source event_present "Throttle too high". gps-configuration-rejected source event_present "unable to configure band" or "still configuring", with the contemporaneous fix type and h_acc. compasses-inconsistent-reported source event_present "Compasses inconsistent". Post-incident reports don't establish pre-flight inconsistency. vibration-persistent-pre-event episode persistence Any IMU axis > profile threshold (default 30) for ≥ 2 s, or > 60 for ≥ 1 s, in the pre-event window. clipping-pre-event episode counter_increment Positive clipping-counter increments between consecutive observations ≤ 3 s apart in the pre-event window. Decreases count as resets. vibration-peak-sample series peak A single sample exceeds the threshold. This is a weaker, context-free signal. tracking-loss episode persistence Tilt tracking error > 30° for ≥ 0.5 s before the upset. ekf-compass-innovation-pre-event episode persistence EKF compass test ratio > 1.0 for ≥ 2 s pre-event. Also reports the armed-on-ground value: a rise only under thrust is consistent with motor-current interference. motor-ceiling-saturation episode persistence A motor at its maximum output (MOT_SPIN_MAX) for ≥ 1 s pre-event. motor-floor-saturation-pre-event episode persistence A motor at its minimum airborne output (MOT_SPIN_MIN) for ≥ 2 s pre-event (excluding the first 2 s after takeoff). motor-output-imbalance-pre-event episode motor_balance Spread of mean motor commands > 0.12 of the PWM range. Decomposed into roll/pitch/yaw using the frame geometry; flags predominantly yaw imbalance. power-monitoring-gap source coverage No battery-voltage samples while armed. Blocks the power hypothesis. batt-monitor-disabled snapshot parameter BATT_MONITOR = 0 (instance 1 only). fs-gcs-disabled snapshot parameter FS_GCS_ENABLE = 0. Context, not a fault. arming-skipchk-board-voltage snapshot parameter ARMING_SKIPCHK bit 7 set. Only assessed under the Copter 4.7.2 semantic pack. profile-parameter-mismatch snapshot profile_parameters Observed values differ from the profile's expected parameters.

docs.title: Derived indicators used by rules
docs.text:
• Tilt tracking error: the angle between the thrust vectors implied by desired and estimated roll/pitch, paired within 0.25 s. It matches the meaning of Copter's crash-check AngErr, but uses telemetry-rate samples.
  • Motor mapping: SERVOn_FUNCTION 33–40 → motor 1–8. Floor and ceiling come from MOT_PWM_MIN/MAX and MOT_SPIN_MIN/MAX. Frames: QUAD/X and QUAD/+. Other frames are mapped but not decomposed.
  • Mixer decomposition: a weighted difference of motor commands (right−left, front−back, CCW−CW props). A sustained negative ccw_minus_cw means the CW-prop motors work harder, which corresponds to sustained yaw torque demand.

docs.title: Hypothesis ranking
docs.text:
Hypotheses are defined in the same YAML and ranked only for episodes with a crash report:

Hypothesis Supported by (family, weight) Contradicted by Estimator/magnetic inconsistency compass-event-before-crash (estimator, 1), ekf-compass-innovation (magnetic, 1), compasses-inconsistent (magnetic, 0.25) tilt tracking error preceded the compass event (1) Mechanical/thrust or frame configuration tracking-loss (control, 1), motor-floor (propulsion, 1), motor-imbalance (propulsion, 0.75), motor-ceiling (propulsion, 0.5) none Vibration-driven estimation degradation vibration-persistent (inertial, 1), clipping (inertial, 1) vibration or clipping assessed and not triggered pre-event (0.5 each) Electrical/power degradation none blocked by power-monitoring-gap 
score = Σ_family min(family_cap = 1.5, Σ weights of triggered rules in that family) − Σ contradiction weights
label = unassessable      if blocked, or no supporting rule could be assessed
        mixed support     if both support and contradictions exist
        strong support    score ≥ 2
        some support      score ≥ 1
        weak support      score > 0
        limited or contradicting evidence otherwise

Capping by family stops repeated or correlated observations (e.g. three vibration axes) from piling up. The weights are expert screening choices, not calibrated likelihoods. Each hypothesis lists the observation that would best discriminate it, for example onboard XKF4 innovations, ESC telemetry or a props-off motor test.

docs.title: Mission statuses
docs.text:
Transactions (upload, download, partial_write, clear, item_read) are reconstructed with direction, broadcast-ACK matching, retransmit counting and restart detection. Plan versions carry a confidence level: confirmed_by_ack, observed_onboard, derived_from_baseline (a partial write onto a known plan) or uncertain (an interrupted or rejected overwrite, since ArduPilot uploads are not atomic).

For each plan item in the episode's latest prior version:

Status Meaning reported_complete A MISSION_ITEM_REACHED for that sequence was received during the episode. geometry_consistent_with_completion The nearest recorded position is within WP_RADIUS_M plus GPS h_acc. This is not proof. completion_not_observed No report, and either no position coverage or a non-positional item (takeoff, RTL). not_visited_in_observed_trajectory Position coverage has no gaps over 5 s, and the nearest approach is outside the margin. unassessable Nothing to compare.

docs.title: Firmware semantic packs
docs.text:
telemetry_platform/semantics/*.yaml:

  • ardupilot-common: C-cast parameter encoding (validated for integrality and type range) and volatile counters (STAT_*) that are not reported as configuration changes.
  • arducopter-4.7.2: matched by version string and, when present, the git hash in ArduCopter V4.7.2 (fb773567). A different hash is reported as a probable custom build. The pack holds parameter descriptions, bitmasks and crash-check semantics.

docs.title: Data-quality diagnostics
docs.text:
Shown in the Limitations section of the manifest and in the web UI's diagnostics list:

Kind Meaning invalid_frame MAVLink CRC or decoding failure. The frame is excluded and the parser resyncs. recovered_span / unrecovered_tail Bytes skipped during resync. truncated Incomplete final frame. The dataset is marked partial. unknown_definition / unsupported_flags Excluded rather than trusted. capture_clock_regression / possible_boot_reset / boot_counter_wrap Clock discontinuities that split the data into epochs. incomplete_text / conflicting_text STATUSTEXT chunk reassembly problems. dataflash_tail DFReader stopped before the end of the file. series_limit The in-memory derived-indicator cap was reached, so later samples were not assessed.

docs.title: Writing a rule
docs.text:
1. Add an entry to rules/core.yaml using an existing detector type: event_present, event_sequence, persistence, counter_increment, peak, motor_balance, coverage, parameter or profile_parameters.
  2. Give it an id, an integer version, severity, per scope, detail / detail_not_triggered templates and missing.
  3. Add a synthetic test in test_engine.py, and if possible a simulator scenario that exercises it.
  4. Bump the pack version. Old analyses keep the pack hash they were produced with.

Rules can't execute code. The loader rejects unknown detector types and duplicate ids.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Telemetry is usually 2–10 Hz. Persistence below the sample interval is reported as unassessable.
  • No cross-file clock alignment yet (a tlog and a .bin are analysed separately).
  • No per-core EKF primary-lane tracking, ESC telemetry rules or PX4 ULog support.
  • Desired attitude in a tlog comes from NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT, which may differ from the rate controller's target.
  • Hypothesis weights are uncalibrated. Treat the order as a prompt for which evidence to check first.

docs.title: AnaTele Preflight: one-button calibration and pre-flight checklist
docs.text:
AnaTele Preflight runs the bench checks and calibrations you would normally do in a ground control station before a flight. One button, Run full preflight, does them in order. It stops when it needs you to move the vehicle, and it writes a timestamped report when it finishes.

Preflight talks to a live vehicle

The rest of AnaTele is read-only. It only reads log files. Preflight is the only part that opens a MAVLink connection to a vehicle and sends commands. It runs as a separate tool (anatele preflight, or Tools → Preflight checklist… in the desktop app, which opens its own window and process).

  • Calibrations overwrite the vehicle's stored calibration (gyro, barometer, level trim, compass offsets, accelerometer offsets and scales). Reboot the vehicle after compass or accelerometer calibration.
  • Preflight never arms the vehicle. It refuses to start if the vehicle is armed. If the vehicle becomes armed during the run, the run stops.
  • The motor test spins motors. It only runs when you tick Props removed, and the GUI asks you to confirm that again. In the terminal you must type props off. Remove every propeller first.
  • Every wait has a timeout, and Abort stops the run at the next check.

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text:
# Step What happens Needs you? 1 Connect and heartbeat Waits for HEARTBEAT, then reads the vehicle type, autopilot and firmware (AUTOPILOT_VERSION). Refuses to continue if armed. No 2 Gyro and barometer calibration MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_CALIBRATION with param1=1 (gyro), then param3=1 (baro ground pressure), each waiting for COMMAND_ACK. Keep it still 3 Level (board) calibration MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_CALIBRATION param5=2. Sets the AHRS trim from the current attitude. Keep it level and still 4 Compass calibration (guided) MAV_CMD_DO_START_MAG_CAL (all compasses, retry, autosave). Shows MAG_CAL_PROGRESS per compass and the MAG_CAL_REPORT result (status, fitness). Cancel sends MAV_CMD_DO_CANCEL_MAG_CAL. Rotate the vehicle 5 Accelerometer 6-position (guided) MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_CALIBRATION param5=1. Follows the vehicle's MAV_CMD_ACCELCAL_VEHICLE_POS requests (LEVEL, LEFT, RIGHT, NOSE DOWN, NOSE UP, BACK). Next confirms each position. Place the vehicle 6 ways 6 Pre-arm health Sends MAV_CMD_RUN_PREARM_CHECKS and collects SYS_STATUS sensor health, EKF_STATUS_REPORT flags and variances, GPS_RAW_INT fix, satellites and HDOP, battery (SYS_STATUS/BATTERY_STATUS), RC_CHANNELS and every PreArm: message. No 7 Motor test (props off) MAV_CMD_DO_MOTOR_TEST for each motor in turn, at 6 % throttle (1 to 15 % allowed) for 2 s. Multicopters only. Skipped unless "Props removed" is ticked. Confirm order and direction 8 Parameters vs profile Reads the parameters in your profile (PARAM_REQUEST_READ, or PARAM_REQUEST_LIST for large profiles) and reports mismatches. No

Each step ends as PASS, WARN, FAIL, SKIPPED or NEEDS_USER, with a one-line message. NEEDS_USER means a guided step was cancelled or had nobody to answer it. The overall result is the worst step result. A failed step does not stop the run (except for a failed connection or an armed vehicle). You see everything in one pass.

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
You usually don't need a connection string. Auto-detect is the default. It lists the serial ports, puts anything that looks like a flight controller first (USB vendor ids of ArduPilot/ChibiOS boards, or "ArduPilot", "Pixhawk", "Cube" in the name), then USB-serial radios, and finally listens on UDP 14550. It picks the first one that sends an autopilot HEARTBEAT. While scanning it only listens; nothing is sent until a vehicle answers. Bluetooth serial ports are skipped because opening them can hang; choose one by hand if your radio uses Bluetooth.

anatele preflight --list-ports   # what auto-detect would see, flight controller first
Link Connection string Notes Auto-detect auto (default) Scans USB serial, then udpin:0.0.0.0:14550. USB (Windows) COM3 Baud is ignored for native USB, but 115200 is the usual value. Close Mission Planner/QGC first; only one program can open the port. USB (Linux/macOS) /dev/ttyACM0, /dev/tty.usbmodem* You may need to be in the dialout group. Telemetry radio COM5 with baud 57600 SiK radios default to 57600. UDP (listen) udpin:0.0.0.0:14550 For SITL, MAVProxy --out, or a companion computer/Wi-Fi bridge sending to this PC. UDP (send) udpout:192.168.4.1:14550 When the vehicle side listens. TCP tcp:127.0.0.1:5760 SITL's default TCP port. Simulated sim: (or --simulate) A built-in fake ArduCopter. Try the whole flow with no hardware.

Preflight asks the vehicle for telemetry streams (REQUEST_DATA_STREAM), because some links stream nothing until a ground station asks.

docs.title: Using the window
docs.text:
anatele preflight                      # opens the Preflight window (auto-detect selected)
anatele preflight --connect COM3       # pre-selects a port
anatele preflight --simulate           # simulated vehicle

You can also open it from the desktop app: Tools → Preflight checklist….

  1. The Connection list shows Auto-detect, every detected serial port (flight controllers first), UDP 14550 and the simulated vehicle. Leave it on Auto-detect, pick a port, or type any connection string. Refresh re-scans after you plug the board in. Press Connect, or press Run full preflight straight away; it connects first.
  2. Optional: Load profile… to compare parameters, and tick Props removed if you want the motor test.
  3. Press Run full preflight. The checklist table fills in with coloured statuses, the progress bar shows the current step, and the log pane shows every vehicle message.
  4. When a guided step needs you, the Action needed bar appears with the instruction and Next / Cancel (or Yes / No) buttons.
  5. When the run finishes, the report is saved automatically to ~/AnaTele Preflight/. Export report… saves another copy to any folder.

docs.title: Using the terminal
docs.text:
anatele preflight --no-gui                      # auto-detect
anatele preflight --no-gui --connect COM3
anatele preflight --no-gui --connect udpin:0.0.0.0:14550 --profile quad.json --report-dir reports
anatele preflight --no-gui --connect COM3 --props-removed          # asks you to type "props off"
anatele preflight --no-gui --simulate --skip compass accel
anatele preflight --no-gui --connect COM3 --save-profile quad.json  # save current parameters as a profile
Option Meaning --connect STR Connection string (see the table above); default auto --list-ports List serial ports, likely flight controller first, and exit --baud N Serial baud rate (default 115200) --simulate Use the built-in simulated vehicle --no-gui Run in the terminal. Guided steps prompt there: Enter = Next/Yes, n = No, c = Cancel --profile FILE Parameter profile to compare against --save-profile FILE Download the current parameters, save them as a profile, then exit --report-dir DIR Where to write the report (default ~/AnaTele Preflight) --skip STEP … Skip steps: gyro_baro, level, compass, accel, health, motors, params --props-removed Allow the motor test (confirmed again by typing props off) --motor-throttle P Motor-test throttle in percent, 1 to 15 (default 6)

The exit code is 0 when the overall result is PASS or WARN and 1 otherwise. That makes it usable in scripts.

docs.title: Gyro, barometer and level
docs.text: Put the vehicle on a level, stable surface and don't touch it. Preflight asks you once to confirm that it is still. Gyro calibration takes a few seconds. The barometer calibration sets the current pressure as ground level. Level calibration stores the current attitude as "level" (AHRS trim). ArduPilot refuses trims over 10°. Do the accelerometer calibration first on a new board; level calibration only fine-tunes it.

docs.title: Compass calibration
docs.text:
1. Take the vehicle away from metal, cars, reinforced concrete, laptops and phone chargers. Fit the battery if it is near the compass in flight.
  2. When the prompt appears, pick the vehicle up and slowly rotate it so that each side (top, bottom, nose, tail, left, right) points at the ground in turn. A smooth "figure of eight" while turning around yourself works well.
  3. Progress for each compass is shown in percent. When every compass has reported, the step shows the status and fitness (lower is better) for each one.
  4. A failed compass is retried automatically by the vehicle. If it still fails, the step is FAIL. Check the compass orientation (COMPASS_ORIENT) and move further from interference.
  5. Results are saved automatically on success. Reboot the vehicle to use the new offsets.

Cancel stops the calibration on the vehicle and keeps the previous calibration.

docs.title: Accelerometer 6-position calibration
docs.text:
The vehicle drives this calibration: it asks for each position in turn, and the prompt follows it.

  1. Place the vehicle in the position shown and hold it completely still: level, on its LEFT side, on its RIGHT side, nose DOWN, nose UP, on its BACK.
  2. Press Next. The vehicle samples for about a second and then asks for the next position.
  3. After the sixth position the vehicle reports success or failure. On success, reboot the vehicle.

If you cancel half-way, the vehicle keeps waiting for positions until it reboots. Reboot it to abandon the calibration.

docs.title: Pre-arm health
docs.text:
Preflight listens to telemetry for a few seconds, asks the vehicle to run its pre-arm checks, and then reports:

  • FAIL: an enabled sensor reports unhealthy, pre-arm checks are failing (any PreArm: message), the EKF has no attitude, or an EKF variance is 0.8 or higher.
  • WARN: no 3D GPS fix, fewer than 6 satellites, HDOP above 2, EKF variance from 0.5 to 0.8, battery below 30 %, battery or RC data missing.

docs.title: Motor test
docs.text:
Only for multicopters, and only with Props removed ticked. The motor count comes from FRAME_CLASS (4 is assumed if unknown). Each motor spins in turn at low throttle for 2 s, in test order A, B, C… (clockwise from front right on most frames). Afterwards you are asked whether the order and direction were right. Compare them with the ArduPilot motor-order diagram for your frame.

The vehicle refuses the test if it is not landed, the board is still initialising, or RC is not calibrated. The vehicle's reason is shown.

docs.title: Parameter profiles
docs.text:
A profile is a JSON file:

{
  "name": "my-quad",
  "tolerance": 0.0001,
  "params": {"FRAME_CLASS": 1, "FRAME_TYPE": 1, "BATT_LOW_VOLT": 14.0, "FS_THR_ENABLE": 1}
}

Save current as profile… (or --save-profile) downloads every parameter and keeps the ones that matter for safety: FRAME_*, BATT_*, FS_*, FENCE_*, RTL_*, ARMING_*, MOT_SPIN_*, MOT_PWM_*, MOT_BAT_*, THR_FS*, RC_FS* and BRD_SAFETY*. Edit the file to add or remove parameters. Values are compared with a relative tolerance (default 1e-4). Missing parameters are a WARN, and differing values are a FAIL.

Preflight never writes parameters except for the calibration values the vehicle saves itself.

docs.title: Simulate mode
docs.text: --simulate (or connection sim:) uses a built-in fake ArduCopter. It answers like the real firmware: ACKs, compass progress and reports, accelerometer position requests, telemetry, parameters and motor-test ACKs. Use it to learn the flow or to demo the tool. The test suite (test_preflight.py) uses the same simulator.

docs.title: Report format
docs.text:
Each run writes preflight-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json and .md to the report folder.

{
  "tool": "AnaTele Preflight",
  "anatele_version": "0.5.0",
  "started": "2026-10-30T18:40:02+0530",
  "finished": "2026-10-30T18:47:31+0530",
  "connection": "COM3 @ 115200",
  "vehicle": {"vehicle_type": "QUADROTOR", "autopilot": "ARDUPILOTMEGA", "firmware": "4.6.3 (official)", "system_id": 1},
  "overall": "WARN",
  "props_removed_confirmed": true,
  "profile": "my-quad",
  "steps": [
    {"id": "connect", "title": "Connect and heartbeat", "status": "PASS", "message": "…", "details": {}, "duration_s": 1.2}
  ]
}

The Markdown file has the same content as a table, followed by the details for each step (compass fitness and offsets, accelerometer positions, EKF variances, GPS, battery, PreArm messages, parameter mismatches). A report is a checklist record. It is not an airworthiness approval.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom What to try No HEARTBEAT within 10 s Wrong port or baud; another program (Mission Planner, QGC, MAVProxy) holds the port; radio not linked; for UDP, check the firewall and that the vehicle sends to this PC. Vehicle is ARMED Disarm with your transmitter or GCS. Preflight never disarms or arms. Gyro calibration FAILED The vehicle moved. Leave it still on a stable surface and run again. Level calibration FAILED / trim over maximum The vehicle is more than 10° off level, or the accelerometers are not calibrated yet. Do the accelerometer calibration first. Compass: no MAG_CAL_PROGRESS The EXTRA3 stream is disabled on that link (SRn_EXTRA3 = 0). Raise it, or use USB. Compass fitness high / FAILED Move away from metal and electronics. Check COMPASS_ORIENT, and try COMPASS_CAL_FIT only if you understand the trade-off. Accelerometer stops asking for positions The calibration timed out or the vehicle moved while sampling. Reboot the vehicle and repeat. Motor test refused: not landed / RC not calibrated Calibrate the radio. Make sure the vehicle is on the ground and disarmed. Health WARN no RC_CHANNELS The receiver is not connected or bound, or RC_PROTOCOLS excludes it. Everything is slow over the radio Long-range radios are slow. Parameter download uses single reads unless the profile has more than 40 entries.

docs.title: Verified and not verified
docs.text: The command parameters and the guided-calibration flow follow the ArduPilot sources (GCS_Common.cpp, AP_AccelCal.cpp, AP_Compass_Calibration.cpp, CompassCalibrator.cpp, Copter motor_test.cpp). The automated tests run against the simulated vehicle. Behaviour on your firmware version, board and link may differ. Watch the first runs on real hardware closely, and keep your ground control station available as the reference tool.
